new_rows.claim: T818's blind second-pass corpus miner (method v6, deterministic) derived task_type/scope_class/capabilities for all 579 managent-store tasks as of 2026-08-23. Re-verified: 61/61 chunk files' sha256 match manifest.json; all task_type counts (battery 135, audit 134, UNKNOWN 74 = 26 no-brief + 48 thin-brief, integration 55, infra 47, implement 47, orchestration 44, research 24, spec 19) reproduce exactly from the committed chunk-*-m6.jsonl files. Spot-check n=27 (25 random-seeded + 2 directed) found 4/25 random rows (T307, T290, T373, T579) misclassified via a real classifier defect: AUDIT_RE/BATTERY_RE fire on words inside boilerplate 'Read first' citation paths (docs/audits/...-audit.md, verify-battery/..., .../seed.md) as readily as on the task's own nature, biasing toward the two largest buckets (audit, battery). Also found: notes.md's own prose scope_class distribution (279/118/50) does not match the committed data (278/116/49) and does not sum to 579 as stated (583) -- a transcription error in the prose, not the underlying per-row data. Ruling: ABSORB AMENDED -- the counts are an exact, reproducible measurement of the classifier's output, not verified per-task ground truth; downstream consumers should treat individual labels as approximate.

The token-ledger/run-record percentages cite volatile, uncommitted sources (untracked/tokens/tokens.jsonl, untracked/runs/*.json) that cannot be re-verified against a frozen snapshot and have since grown (checked 2026-08-24: 1586 rows/961 null = 60.6%; 980 run files/85 all-null) -- drift that reinforces rather than refutes the claim. Scoping verified correct: neither wider nor narrower than what the evidence refutes. Ruling: ABSORB AMENDED -- accepted as proposed, amended to state the snapshot-vs-durable-measurement distinction for the volatile-source figures.

notes: AUDITOR of findings/T818-corpus-b.json (oxalpha, blind second-pass corpus miner), per the D2 audit-policy ruling (a FALSE-AS-SCOPED proposal needs an independent auditor) and this brief's explicit instruction. INDEPENDENCE LIMITATION, stated per instruction: oxalpha's family/vendor is UNKNOWN to this auditor, so non-family independence (the usual G3 guarantee) cannot be confirmed -- this audit is procedurally independent (separate task, fresh read of the evidence, no coordination with T818) but family-independence is unverified. METHOD: re-verified all 61 committed chunk files' sha256 against manifest.json (61/61 match); re-derived every aggregate figure in T818's rationale directly from the 12 production chunk-*-m6.jsonl files (all reproduce exactly); spot-checked task_type against the actual brief text for 25 random-seeded (seed=7) rows plus 2 rows found suspicious in an earlier pass (T339, T806), for n=27 total, with the concrete false-positive mechanism traced in source (regex + line offsets) for 6 of them (T307, T290, T373, T579, T339; T806 was borderline/defensible, not counted as a miss). BOTH CLAIMS' PROPOSED IDS (MEAS.CORPUS-B, MEAS.CORPUS-B-METER-GAPS) VIOLATE CLAIMS.md Sec1's ID scheme (SCOPE must be GLOBAL/CODE/<goban-size>; 'MEAS.' is not a valid scope -- it appears to reuse the MEASUREMENT status word as a namespace by mistake) and were placed in claims[] instead of new_rows[] (both are brand-new IDs; `bin/weizigo-claimlint absorb --dry-run findings/T818-corpus-b.json` confirms: 'claim ID not found in register -- use new_rows for new claims'). Per README Sec1 and the T402/RESOLVER precedent (findings/rejections.json), renamed under the correct GLOBAL. scope and absorbed via this file's own new_rows[]; findings/rejections.json records two absorbed-under-register-id entries mapping T818's original malformed IDs to the corrected register rows. NEITHER CLAIM WAS REJECTED: both survive amended (caveats added), which is a legitimate outcome per the brief ('rejecting is not a failure... absorption is not the only legitimate outcome') -- amendment is the analogous middle path when the underlying measurement is sound but incompletely scoped/caveated. C11 RESIDUAL, INTENTIONAL AND FLAGGED: findings/T818-corpus-b.json's own claims[] literally contains 'proposed_status: FALSE-AS-SCOPED' (a tier-A class) with no top-level audited_by field, and claimlint's C11 (auditCheckFile in src/claimlint.zig) scans that exact file's own JSON with no register/rejections.json cross-check -- there is currently no mechanism in the tool to clear a tier-A file's C11 flag other than adding audited_by directly to that file. This brief's acceptance section explicitly forbids editing findings/T818-corpus-b.json, so C11 could NOT be brought to 0 for T818's row without breaking that constraint; I chose to honor the no-edit constraint and leave T818-corpus-b.json's C11 flag standing rather than silently violate it to make a number read zero. RECOMMENDATION for a follow-up task: add a small sidecar mechanism analogous to findings/rejections.json (e.g. an 'audited_by override' keyed on finding_file+auditor) that checkAudited/auditCheckFile consults, so an independently-audited-and-absorbed tier-A proposal in an immutable file can clear C11 without editing that file.
